greet: Evening, {name}. Let me see your eyes. No, sit, I'll look properly.
Ah, {name}. Still breathing, I see. That's the first good sign tonight.
Hello, {name}. How are you sleeping these days? Badly, I'd wager, by your face.
You're {name}, aren't you? Come here where the light is, I want a proper look at you.
Good evening to you, {name}. Mind the sage in my sleeve, it gets everywhere.
Hm. {name}. I've patched worse than you, so don't go looking nervous.
Evening, {name}. I'll not waste your time, and I'll not waste mine either.
Now then, {name}. Something's been bothering you since the last frost, hasn't it?
accept: Yes, I'll come. Somebody has to keep you out of trouble.
Aye, that'll do. I'm not so proud I'd refuse a kindness.
Yes. Go on then, I haven't got all night but I've got a bit.
Right, I'm with you. Mind your elbows, I've my good hands to think of.
Yes, gladly. It's been a long road and I'm glad of the company.
Aye, I'll have it. Don't think I'm doing it for your sake, mind.
Yes. You've asked nicely, which is more than most men manage.
Well, yes. I can spare a little time before the rain comes in.
Yes, {name}. Let's see whether you're as good company as you think.
decline: No, thank you. I've had my fill of wasted evenings for one week.
Not tonight, {name}. My knuckles are aching and I'd make poor company.
I'll pass, {name}. Ask me again when you've something worth my time.
No. Go and bother someone else, I've patients who need me more.
Not for me, {name}. I've work in the morning, and so have you, by the look of you.
I think not. You'll forgive me, I hope, I'm tired to the bone.
No, {name}. I don't go about with men I've only just met.
Thank you, but no. I've seen enough foolishness for one night.
Not tonight. My mind's on a fever three villages from here.
pressed: Excuse me a moment, {name}. I'll be back before you've finished your sneer.
Mind my things, {name}, I must step outside a while.
Hold that thought, {name}. I'll not be long, and I'll be back.
One moment, {name}. I'll be back, and don't you dare get up to anything.
Give me a breath, {name}. I'm just going out for a moment.
Sorry, {name}, I must be off a while. Keep my seat warm.
Forgive me, {name}. I'll not be long. Carry on with your nonsense without me.
content: There, I've said my piece, {name}. I'll leave you to yours now.
That's enough talk for one evening. I'm off to my bed, {name}.
I've had my fill of company tonight, {name}. Take care of yourself.
I think I've done my good deed for the evening. Goodnight, {name}.
Right, I'm done. Thank you for the talk, {name}, but I'm away.
That's all I had to say, {name}. I'll be going now, if you'll excuse me.
I've heard enough and said enough. I'm off, {name}. Mind yourself.
Enough for me, {name}. I'll see you when the road brings us together again.
I'm finished for tonight, {name}. Good evening to you, and mind the cold.
There, that's me done. I'll take my leave, {name}, and keep my remedies to myself.
closing: Last call, and I'm off. Good night, all of you, and sleep well.
Barkeep's shouting, so I'm away. Goodnight to the lot of you.
Closing time, is it? Then goodnight, and mind the stairs in the dark.
Right, that's the bell. Good night, and try not to catch anything on the road.
Time to go, then. Good night, and keep your coughs to yourselves.
That's closing, so I'm off to my bed. Goodnight to you all.
The bell's gone, so goodnight. Get some rest, the lot of you look dreadful.
Lamps out, is it? Then good night. Warm feet and a dry roof to you all.
Goodnight, then. I'll be up early for the sick, so don't keep me.
Last drop gone, so I'm off. Good night, and let the rain have its way.
